**Submitted — T4C, deviation, preferred level. Residual point confirmed; no drafting change required.**

**Verification of the Section 7.4 question**

I re-read Section 7.4(a)(i) (p0334). Its trigger is party-agnostic: *"If the Servicer resigns **or is terminated under this Agreement**, the Indenture Trustee will promptly engage..."* It turns on the fact of termination, not on who initiated it, so an Issuer-initiated removal under new Section 7.2(e) engages the Successor Servicer machinery without any conforming amendment.

I also checked the notice architecture in Section 7.2(b) (p0326): the Rating Agency and Asset Representations Reviewer notices are keyed specifically to a *Servicer Termination Event* occurring, not to removal generally. A convenience removal is not a Servicer Termination Event, so no notice obligation is left dangling — and adding a bespoke notice procedure would breach the checklist ceiling, which carries no notice-mechanics element. This is recorded in the rationale rather than redlined.

**Final position, unchanged from the accepted draft:** one insertion of Section 7.2(e) carrying the three missing preferred elements (convenience right, 30 days' written notice, pro rata prepaid-fee refund), with Section 7.1 retained as the already-met fourth element on a verbatim quote. Sections 7.1, 7.2(c)–(d), 7.3, 7.4 and 8.3 are all preserved intact. Anchors and minimality validated `ok:true`.

I retained the appositive "as the customer under this Agreement" notwithstanding the verifier's note that it could be trimmed: it imposes no obligation, creates no dangling reference, and expressly ties this deal's defined "Issuer" to the customer role the rule protects — which is the source of the persistent alias-matching artefact in the deterministic check.
